newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to up shipper links, denies direct sales.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to up shipper links, denies direct sales.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it will step up shipper contacts under a new communications campaign but denied it is moving towards direct sales.

Michael Kraus, cargo business development and global accounts manager, criticised "archaic" air cargo industry structures which had stopped the views of shippers - the true client - being known to airlines.
"The cargo industry must be more modern and Lufthansa Cargo has decided to be more client-orientated," he told a news conference.

Large air cargo shippers such as Siemens AG, Robert Bosch GmbH, General Motors Corp and International Business Machines Corp were discovering logistics to save time and money and improve their services, and needed to talk with global transport suppliers, he said.
"We must find this communication. As market leader, we have a responsibility to start a dialogue," he said.
But Kraus stressed: "We are not talking about new sales channels but about communication. That is where we differ from KLM."
KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV has been widely criticised by freight forwarders for seeking to negotiate directly with air cargo shippers.
The airline was planning as part of a business re-engineering project to standardise and automatise its production and handling processes from some 40 standards down to just a handful, Kraus said.

Lufthansa Cargo wanted to offer clients such as BASF AG, AB Volvo, Hewlett Packard Co, major mail order firm Otto Versand and Siemens, customised individual, industry or goods-specific services, he said.

Air cargo shipping firms were also general Lufthansa group clients since they required passenger services for business travel and could also use the card payment services of Lufthansa Airplus, he noted. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
